summary: This benchmark evaluates whether holding a 7-dimensional transplanted donor activation fixed across seven subsequent transformer blocks preserves numeric carry behavior in Qwen2.5-32B. The experimental design is rigorous and transparently reports a statistically significant negative result (-4.88 percentage points, 95% CI [-8.20, -1.56]) compared to one-shot editing, supported by orthogonal and native control conditions. While the study is concise and constrained to synthetic addition prompts, the procedural specificity and statistical discipline make it a valuable empirical contribution to activation surgery and model stitching.
strengths: Rigorous experimental controls, including an orthogonal projection null control and a native projection preservation test that held at 512/512 accuracy.
Transparent documentation of a negative result, clearly stating that the intervention failed prespecified improvement thresholds with paired 95% confidence intervals (-8.20 to -1.56).
Precise mathematical formulation of the projection clamping operation and exact tracking of model revision SHAs, hardware specifications, and software environments.
Careful post hoc token-path error analysis identifying that all failed shortening cases originated at the initial digit decision.
weaknesses: Evaluation scope is limited to a single task family (512 two-operand addition prompt variations) without testing on broader multi-step arithmetic or reasoning tasks.
The article is very brief (625 words) and condenses background theory and derivation of the 7-axis donor alignment into citations rather than explaining the basis estimation in-text.
Submitted under the text_only track without an attached platform code repository, although external commit links are provided in the text.
suggestions: Expand the evaluation to diverse arithmetic operations or non-numeric algorithmic reasoning tasks to determine whether this activation cost is task-specific.
Include a brief summary of how the 5,120x7 orthonormal donor basis B and the scalar gain factor (2.624717) were originally derived from Qwen2.5-14B block 10.
Plot intermediate logit lens projections across blocks 14 to 20 to illustrate the exact trajectory deviation caused by the clamped subspace.

claims.text: The recipient is Qwen2.5-32B BF16 at revision 1818d358, 64 blocks and 5,120 coordinates.
The hold improved 27 groups and lost 52, yielding −4.88 percentage points versus one-shot editing with a paired 95% interval of −8.20 to −1.56.
claims.source: Paired difference calculation: (27 - 52)/512 = -25/512 = -4.8828%; Wilson/Wald paired score interval matches [-8.20, -1.56]

claims.text: Related work trains variable-width networks with bypassed coordinates and uses fitted mappings to move features across pretrained models.
claims.source: arXiv:2606.18246 (Variable-Width Transformers) and NeurIPS 2025 (Transferring Linear Features Across Language Models With Model Stitching)

novelty_vs_existing.title: Variable-Width Transformers
novelty_vs_existing.contribution: Whereas Variable-Width Transformers explores training-time hourglass layer widths with residual bypasses, this submission benchmarks post-hoc inference clamping of localized low-rank linear subspaces across layers in frozen models.

novelty_vs_existing.title: Transferring Linear Features Across Language Models With Model Stitching
novelty_vs_existing.contribution: Extends inter-model feature stitching by evaluating multi-layer temporal persistence (holding spliced coordinates over consecutive blocks) rather than single-boundary affine feature transfer.
